candidates.content_text:
At City of Newcastle (CN), you won't just design roads, drainage networks, cycleways and recreational infrastructure, you'll help create the places where our community lives, works and connects. This is an exciting opportunity to bring your technical expertise, creativity and project management skills to a role that delivers lasting outcomes for one of Australia's most vibrant and evolving cities.
As a member of our team, you won't just work for the city; you’ll co-create it. Here, your ideas and efforts directly shape the places where you and your community live, work, and play.
We currently have two permanent Civil Designer opportunities available within our team.
As a Civil Designer, you will take a lead role in the design and delivery of a diverse range of civil infrastructure projects. From initial investigations and concept development through to detailed design, approvals and construction support, you will be responsible for producing high-quality design documentation that transforms ideas into community assets.
Working collaboratively across the organisation and with external stakeholders, you will manage the design process, coordinate consultants and contractors, and oversee project budgets through the design and approval phases. You will provide technical advice during construction, work through complex design challenges and help ensure projects are delivered safely, sustainably and cost-effectively.
This role offers the opportunity to influence the future of Newcastle by delivering infrastructure that improves connectivity, enhances public spaces and supports a growing city. You'll apply your expertise to project investigations, design development, cost estimates, environmental assessments and planning approvals while ensuring compliance with relevant standards, legislation and best-practice design principles.
Beyond project delivery, you'll play an important role in strengthening capability across the team by sharing your knowledge, supporting less experienced designers and contributing to innovation and continuous improvement. You'll help foster a collaborative environment where safety, excellence and creative problem-solving are valued and encouraged.
We're looking for motivated and forward-thinking professionals who combine strong technical design skills with the ability to build relationships, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes. Through your work, you’ll have a behind the scenes pass to Newcastle's evolution as you shape our future as a liveable, inclusive city.
Life at City of Newcastle (CN) 
You’ll get to experience your work up close alongside the brilliant minds of your colleagues who care for one another and the region.
You’ll chip away at ambitious plans with a talented, passionate crew alongside you, shaping the very fabric of our community. Showing up for neighbours not shareholders.
Every single day offers the chance to think big and act local. Planning and prioritising to achieve the most important outcomes with the community.
You’ll add value in the moments that matter. From librarians to lifeguards, in a range of iconic places, we achieve a better Newcastle together.
Whether we’re planning to host major events, providing essential services or supporting creative artists, it’s what we do when the cameras aren't rolling that matters most.
And we’ll be there for you in important times in your life. We embrace flexible work arrangements to find a balance that allows us to enjoy the city we shape.
Our focus on inclusion and respecting culture, will help you feel a deeper connection with others. You'll connect with internal communities that will help you to feel a sense of belonging and reflect the diversity of the growing region.
You’ll do meaningful work and do it sustainably as you take ideas from plan to play, in your own backyard.
With hundreds of different roles, each person adds their uniqueness to our culture and plays their part as we head towards our 2040 vision.
With natural assets and a focus on the environment, co-create a sustainable region with us.
Why join CN? 
At CN, we value our employees, and their wellbeing takes priority. We encourage employees to make time for what's important and provide the benefits to enable a work life balance that allow us to enjoy the city we shape. To read more, visit here!

We champion inclusion so that everyone is valued, and we encourage innovation and creativity. We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive workplace where different styles, backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are valued, encouraged, and respected.
People with diverse lived experiences (including but not limited to, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians, people with diverse gender identities and sexualities, people from different cultural, racial, ethnic, religious and linguistic backgrounds, people with disability, carers, and veterans) are encouraged to apply.
Don’t just work for the city, co-create it. Join and expand your career at the City of Newcastle.

candidates.content_text:
Civil Designer (Ref: 1350)
About the position:
The Civil Designer prepares concept and detailed designs, drawings, quantity schedules, cost estimates, and supporting technical documentation for the City’s capital works and infrastructure programs. The role undertakes investigations and design development for transport, parks and open space, and utility infrastructure assets, ensuring designs are safe, practical, constructable, maintainable, compliant and fit for purpose. Working under general direction, the position provides technical design advice, contributes to project scoping and option assessment, liaises with internal and external stakeholders to obtain design inputs, and maintains accurate design and handover records.
Key accountabilities:
- Review project briefs and available asset, survey, geotechnical, environmental and service information to identify information gaps. Undertake site inspections and engineering investigations, and develop an appropriate design approach, program and estimate of design effort.
- Prepare concept and detailed designs for municipal infrastructure including earthworks, roads, intersections, roundabouts, car parks, footpaths, shared paths, kerbing, stormwater drainage, culverts and associated civil works, using the City’s approved design and drafting systems.
- Prepare and document relevant design calculations, drawings, schedules of quantities, cost estimates, technical specifications, design reports, approvals information and other documentation required for grant applications, procurement and construction.
For further information and to view the position description, visit www.cgg.wa.gov.au/employment/.
To gain a better understanding of the role, please call Trevor Pitt, Coordinator Design on (08) 9956 6650.
Position requirements:
The successful applicant will ideally hold a Degree in Civil Engineering. Applicants with lesser qualification but significant experience in the design and drafting of reads, footpaths, drainage and other minor scale civil infrastructure works will also be considered. Experience in writing grant applications would be highly regarded.
Completion of a pre-employment medical including alcohol and other substances testing is required of all positions at the City.
Remuneration and benefits:
This position offers a salary starting from $92,692 per annum or $104,203 per hour, commensurate with the successful applicant’s knowledge, skills, experience and qualifications.
Some of the additional benefits of working for the City include:
- Up to 21% Superannuation (with superannuation co-contribution scheme)
- 22 Annual Leave days per annum
- Health & Wellbeing Program
- Flexible working arrangements
- Career opportunities
- Study Assistance
- Centrally located
- Free parking
About the City
Overlooking the Indian Ocean, Geraldton is a thriving regional city at the heart of Australia's Coral Coast. With a growing population of over 41,000 people it offers a wide range of services and activities. Geraldton is recognised as one of WA's key growth areas and the opportunities in this regional city are plentiful. You can be part of working with us to deliver the best for our community and this region.
The City of Greater Geraldton actively welcomes, includes and values the unique contributions of all people in its workplace. The City welcomes applications from all age groups, people with a disability, and those from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer with strong commitment to fitness for work and safety in the workplace.
Interested in applying?
Visit the City’s website: www.cgg.wa.gov.au/employment/ to apply for this position.
To be considered for this vacancy, applicants are advised to include the following:
- A current resume
- A written response (maximum 1250 characters per criteria) addressing the following selection criteria inclusive of examples to support your claims:
i. Degree in Civil Engineering, Diploma in Civil Construction Design, Civil Engineering, Civil and Structural Engineering, or lesser relevant discipline qualifications and substantial civil design experience
ii. Demonstrated competency in relevant civil design and drafting software, including 12d Model and AutoCAD and/or Civil 3D, with demonstrated ability to become proficient in the City’s adopted systems
iii. Demonstrated experience preparing civil engineering designs and drawings for roads, intersections, footpaths, drainage, carparks and related municipal infrastructure
iv. Knowledge of Austroads, Main Roads WA requirements, Australian Rainfall and Runoff, Australian Standards water sensitive urban design and utility coordination
v. High level emotional intelligence, negotiation, problem solving and conflict resolution skills to enable effective liaison with all people at all levels and to persuade others to adopt particular methods or strategies where there are conflicting interests and opinions

 We're seeking individuals with a genuine passion for civil engineering and a strong desire to learn and grow. You'll enjoy working collaboratively with others, communicate effectively, and bring a proactive and enthusiastic approach to your work and study. Most importantly, you'll be eager to contribute to meaningful projects that help shape and support our community.

 The beautiful Eurobodalla Shire is located on Yuin Country on the far south coast of NSW and offers an enviable coastal lifestyle with easy access to Canberra and Sydney. From our beaches to our bushlands, rivers and mountains, the Eurobodalla is a place of inclusive communities embracing sustainable lifestyles.
 With 143km of coastline, 83 beaches, 20 lakes and four major river systems, Eurobodalla is known as the land of many waters. Over three-quarters of our land area is open space, consisting of 10 national parks and 15 state forests.
 Over 40,000 people call the Eurobodalla Shire home, and we attract over 1.2 million visitors every year.
 What we offer
 We promote equal access to opportunities and pride ourselves on creating a safe and engaging working environment that fosters wellbeing. We are dedicated to looking after our staff, knowing our people are our biggest asset, to ensure we are best placed to look after our community. Including benefits such as:
 - 35 hours per week for administrative staff and 38 hours per week for operational staff.
 - Health and wellbeing initiatives including access to free counselling through our Employee Assistance Program, TELUS Health One App, Fitness Passport, Social Club and flu vaccinations.

 - Annual Award increases, performance reviews and a rewards and recognition program.
 - Salary packaging program.
 Application process
 Eurobodalla Shire Council follows a merit based recruitment and selection process. For help and guidance on how to apply for jobs at Council, please visit our website www.esc.nsw.gov.au or The Job Shop. 
 To apply for this position, you will need to:

 - Provide your cover letter highlighting your skills and experience (OPTIONAL)

 - Address the screening questions in the form below.
 If you found this vacancy via a job search website, please go to the Eurobodalla Shire Council Vacant Positions website page to fill in the application form.
 If you have any further questions about the role, please contact Maggie Sale on 0429 123 686.
 Applicants who are currently completing their HSC are encouraged to apply. Applications must be supported by Year 11 and Year 12 results available at the time of submission, including indicative ATAR outcomes or early entry assessment results. Any offer of employment will be subject to the applicant meeting the relevant university entry requirements and providing evidence of enrolment in an approved course.
 Applications close: Sunday 8 November 2026 at 11:00pm.
 Screening process
 Pre‑employment Checks:
 As part of our recruitment process, you will be required to provide contact details for two referees. These will be collected at the interview stage. If you are a recent school leaver (having left school within the last two years), at least one referee should be a teacher, school mentor or other educational representative familiar with your performance and potential. Other referees may include current or former supervisors, employers, sporting coaches, volunteer coordinators or other individuals who can comment on your suitability for the position.
 Depending on the position, successful applicants may also be required to complete a Criminal History Check, Medical Assessment and/or a Working with Children Check.

We are committed to making reasonable adjustments to provide a positive, supportive recruitment process. Please contact us on 02 4474 7378 or via positions@esc.nsw.gov.au for confidential support to ensure an equitable application process.

candidates.content_text:
About Us
Exclusive Construction Machinery and Equipment Pty Ltd is a dynamic and growing civil construction and earthmoving business operating in Western Australia. We specialise in comprehensive earthworks, site preparation, and civil projects that support residential, commercial, and industrial developments. Our projects involve excavation, land clearing, bulk earthworks, trenching, drainage preparation and other essential groundwork that form the critical foundation for infrastructure and building works across the region. Our team works with a modern fleet of machinery and experienced operators to deliver high-quality results safely, efficiently, and on schedule.
Role Overview
We are seeking a motivated Civil Engineering Technician to provide comprehensive technical support to our Civil Engineer across multiple earthworks and site-development projects in Western Australia.
The successful candidate will assist in collecting and analysing site data, preparing and updating engineering drawings, checking completed earthworks against approved drawings and specifications, calculating construction quantities, and preparing technical records and reports. The role combines office-based technical drafting and documentation with regular site attendance for field measurements, construction material testing, technical inspections and quality verification. It supports the accurate implementation and verification of civil engineering works in accordance with approved designs, relevant Australian Standards, project specifications and applicable WHS requirements.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist Civil Engineers in preparing, interpreting and revising civil engineering sketches, technical drawings, plans and technical details for earthworks, site preparation, excavation, trenching and drainage works using AutoCAD and Civil 3D, based on engineering instructions, site measurements and approved design information.
- Prepare and update as-built drawings, drawing registers and associated technical documentation using AutoCAD and Civil 3D to reflect verified site conditions, completed civil engineering works and approved design changes.
- Undertake field measurements and collect site data relating to ground levels, excavation dimensions, earthworks profiles, drainage gradients and site formation to support civil engineering construction activities.
- Analyse and compare field measurements and survey data against approved engineering drawings, design levels, project specifications and applicable technical requirements, identify discrepancies and prepare technical data for review by the Civil Engineer.
- Assist in conducting and coordinating field and laboratory tests of soil and other construction materials, as required, recording results and analysing available test data against project specifications and acceptance criteria.
- Conduct technical inspections of earthworks, excavation, trenching, drainage preparation and site-formation activities, assess completed works against approved drawings and engineering specifications, and document discrepancies and non-conformances for review and rectification.
- Monitor soil placement, filling, backfilling, compaction and drainage works by reviewing field measurements and available material test results, checking completed works against specified engineering requirements and reporting deviations for further assessment.
- Perform technical computations using site measurements, survey information, engineering drawings and relevant technical data to calculate and verify earthworks quantities, excavation and fill volumes, cut-and-fill requirements and construction material quantities.
- Prepare material quantity schedules, earthworks quantity summaries, technical tabulations and supporting tender documentation, and assist in estimating material and labour quantities and costs using engineering drawings, site measurements and relevant construction data.
- Compile and analyse field measurements, survey data, material testing results and inspection findings, and prepare technical reports, data sheets, charts, tabulations, inspection checklists and compliance records for review by the Civil Engineer.
- Check subcontractor drawings, method statements, technical submissions and construction documentation against approved engineering drawings, project specifications and applicable contract requirements, identify technical discrepancies and refer matters requiring engineering judgement or approval to the Civil Engineer.
- Interpret civil engineering work instructions and communicate technical site information, measurement requirements and relevant engineering specifications to site supervisors, machinery operators, subcontractors, surveyors and other project personnel to support the accurate implementation and verification of civil engineering works.
- Maintain accurate technical records of engineering drawings, field measurements, material testing results, inspection findings and project documentation to support technical verification, quality control, compliance reviews and construction handover.
- Identify and document site conditions and technical issues that may affect the quality or compliance of civil engineering construction works, and promptly report discrepancies and matters requiring further technical assessment to the Civil Engineer.
Skills & Qualifications Required
- Diploma or Advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Civil Construction, Building Engineering Technology, or a closely related civil engineering or construction technology discipline. Applicants with other relevant qualifications and substantial, directly relevant civil engineering technical experience may also be considered.
- Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in civil engineering technical support, earthworks, site preparation, drainage works or civil construction.
- Working knowledge of relevant Australian Standards and project specifications applicable to earthworks, soil testing, compaction and site development, including AS 3798 and relevant parts of the AS 1289 series, where applicable.
- Practical competency in AutoCAD and Civil 3D for preparing and updating civil engineering drawings and as-built documentation.
- Ability to interpret civil engineering drawings and specifications, undertake site measurements, record field data and assist with earthworks quantity calculations.
- Understanding of technical inspections, construction quality control, field reporting and documentation of non-conformances.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word. Working knowledge of MS Project is desirable.
- Strong communication and coordination skills when working with Civil Engineers, surveyors, site supervisors, subcontractors and machinery operators.
- Current White Card (Construction Induction Safety Certificate), or willingness and ability to obtain it before commencing site work, where required.
- Valid Australian driver licence, or the ability to obtain an appropriate licence before commencing duties requiring driving, and willingness to travel between project sites across Western Australia as required.
Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, permanent
- Salary: $80,000-90,000 per annum plus superannuation, depending on experience
- Benefits: Travel reimbursement
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shifts, Monday to Friday
What We Offer
- Competitive salary package plus superannuation
- Stable, long-term permanent employment opportunity
- Opportunities for career progression, training and professional development while working alongside experienced Civil Engineers
- Visa sponsorship under the Subclass 482 Skills in Demand visa program may be available to suitably qualified applicants who meet the relevant immigration requirements
- Supportive team culture and modern work systems
- Full personal protective equipment (PPE) and relevant work equipment provided to support role performance
How to Apply
Please click Apply Now to submit your updated resume. Applicants should highlight their relevant civil engineering technical experience, qualifications, software competency and current Australian work rights or visa status.
Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for a confidential interview.

bullets: Long term career opportunity and progression
Competitive salary package
Fast growing company with a supportive culture
candidates.content_text:
A second-generation, family-owned Civil Construction business with a strong professional reputation in the industry and an exciting pipeline of projects is seeking a skilled and capable Site Engineer with previous roadworks and bulk earthworks experience to join our team.
A Civil Engineering Degree together with previous experience as a Site Engineer within the civil construction industry, is essential. We are looking for a Site Engineer who is ready to take ownership, contribute to successful project delivery and build their career within a supportive and professional organisation.
The Site Engineer is the support to the Project Manager and is in control of all project administrative related functions of the job, while working alongside the Site Supervisor with respect to interpreting technical specifications of the project.
The Site Engineer will demonstrate knowledge and practical application of Work Health & Safety, Environmental Management and Quality Systems. The role will provide opportunities to take responsibility for key components across varied projects ranging from working on large-scale TfNSW projects through to smaller industrial subdivisions. Site engineers are required to understand the different needs projects have.
The Site Engineer will assist with monitoring and reporting cost of construction activities tracking they do not exceed the estimated expenses of the project budget against the project program milestones.
The successful applicant must demonstrate the following competencies:
•        Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills
•        Verbal and written communication skills
•        Professional and confident communication with senior management, clients and project stakeholders
•        Ability to plan, prioritise and manage competing workloads and changing deadline
•        Respond to IMS requirements
•        Conversant with civil construction methodologies
•        Numeric plan reading competency
•        TfNSW experience
•        Site administration duties
•        WH&S, Environmental and Quality Support
•        Cross functional support and training   
Why Join Us?
•  Work on diverse and high-profile civil projects that deliver tangible outcomes for the community.
•  Work alongside an experienced and supportive project team that values initiative, collaboration and technical excellence.
• Be part of a professional organisation that is committed to delivering projects to a high standard and striving for “Distinction”.
•  Enjoy an attractive salary package tailored to your experience and expertise.
If you are interested in joining our team and believe your skills and experience align, we welcome the opportunity to hear from you.
Only shortlisted candidates will receive a response to their application. We thank you in advance for your understanding

Build major civil and mining infrastructure projects with a growing industry leader.
We are seeking a motivated and capable Civil Project Engineer to join our team and play a key role in delivering a diverse range of civil construction and mining projects. Working across earthworks, bulk excavation, haul roads, mine infrastructure, drainage, rehabilitation works and associated civil infrastructure, you will provide technical expertise to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on time, and within budget.

- Attend project meetings and provide technical updates.

- Experience delivering bulk earthworks and civil infrastructure projects.
- Current Driver's Licence.
- Strong understanding of construction methodologies and project delivery processes.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
- Sound knowledge of project controls and contract administration.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and project management software.
- Strong analytical, communication and problem-solving skills.
Personal Attributes- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication abilities.
- Proactive, adaptable and solution-focused attitude.
- Genuine commitment to safety, quality and continuous improvement.
Why Join Us?
- Work on large-scale civil construction and mining projects.
- Diverse project portfolio including earthworks, mine infrastructure and rehabilitation works.
- Supportive and experienced leadership team.
- Career development and professional growth opportunities.
- Strong safety-focused culture.
- Competitive remuneration package.
Apply Now
If you're a driven Civil Project Engineer looking to advance your career with a company delivering high-profile civil and mining projects, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply today with your resume and cover letter outlining your relevant experience and project achievements.

About you
- Degree in Civil Engineering, or equivalent experience in civil construction
- Experience on civil, subdivision or council infrastructure projects
- Good knowledge of ITPs, council and Austroads specifications, and NSW WHS requirements
- Organised, with tidy documentation habits and confidence liaising with clients and authorities
- Current driver’s licence and White Card
- Graduates with relevant site experience are welcome to apply

A new, career-making opportunity has arisen for an experienced Project Engineer with a solid track record on FRP (Formwork, Reinforcing & Pouring) projects. This position will initially be based in Loganlea, with future opportunities to support and deliver projects across various locations throughout Brisbane.
Why join us?
- Deliver landmark Brisbane FRP projects that shape the city’s infrastructure
- Join a specialist contractor with a strong reputation and solid project pipeline
- Work with supportive leaders who invest in your development and progression
- Competitive salary package and long-term career stability
About Us
Damcon is one of Australia’s leading FRP (Formwork, Reinforcing & Pouring) specialists, delivering complex bridge and civil infrastructure projects across NSW & QLD.
We pride ourselves on precision, safety, and innovation, and we’ve built long-term relationships by delivering on time and to the highest standards. With a strong pipeline of high-profile projects, we’re looking for a Site Engineer/Project Engineer who wants to be part of a team that delivers challenging FRP packages with excellence.
At Damcon, we’re committed to supporting and developing our people, giving you the tools, mentorship, and opportunities to grow into a future leader in the civil construction industry.
The Role
This is a hands-on role working closely with a Project Manager , Site Supervisors, and the project team to plan, coordinate, and deliver FRP works from start to finish.
You’ll take ownership of formwork sequencing, reinforcement installation, concrete pours, and temporary works, ensuring safety, quality, and program requirements are met, while also managing the commercial and administrative aspects that keep the job running smoothly.
What you'll be doing
- Interpret and review engineering plans and specifications
- Review complex reo/steel schedules
- Review, interpret Temporary works designs
- Plan and coordinate formwork installation, reinforcement placement, and concrete pours in line with project sequencing
- Work alongside Site Supervisors to oversee daily site activities and subcontractor performance
- Conduct FRP quality inspections, complete ITPs, and ensure defects are closed out promptly
- Manage procurement, prepare scopes of work, and coordinate suppliers and deliveries
- Prepare and submit RFIs, variations, EOTs, and payment claims
- Track budgets, forecast costs, and support cash flow planning
- Maintain accurate project records including site diaries, timesheets, and progress reports
- Attend and contribute to internal and client progress meetings, reporting on milestones and challenges
- Liaise with in-house and external drafting teams to review and transmit shop drawings
- Ensure all FRP designs and temporary works comply with engineering requirements and WHS standards
- Proactively identify buildability issues and develop practical solutions with the project team
What we're looking for
- Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or related discipline
- 3+ years’ experience in civil infrastructure with a strong focus on FRP delivery
- Solid understanding of formwork systems, reinforcement detailing, sequencing, and temporary works
- Experience managing subcontractors, budgets, and project documentation on active sites
- White Card and Driver’s License (RIW Card advantageous)
- Excellent problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills
- Optimistic and proactive approach
- Able to work in fast-paced site environments while maintaining quality and safety standards
- Ability to travel to across Brisbane (company car provided upon request).
Apply now
If you’re ready to step into a role where your FRP expertise is valued and your career can grow, send your CV and cover letter. Click the "Apply Now" button to submit your application.

City of Busselton – Where Lifestyle Meets Opportunity

Working at the City of Busselton means job security, work/life balance and a rewarding career at one of the most progressive, diverse and ambitious Local Governments in the state, located in the picturesque southwest coastal region of WA.  We offer: 
- Permanent Full Time and Part Time Roles
- Competitive, negotiable salary depending on skills and experience
- Generous superannuation scheme up to 15.75%
- Financial relocation assistance to eligible applicants
- Excellent employee benefits including the potential to salary package a novated lease vehicle and housing, gym membership, and corporate health discounts
About the role:
As a Civil Designer you will be responsible for providing professional civil engineering design, drafting and project support services for the planning, development and delivery of the City's infrastructure programs. You will prepare engineering designs, specifications, estimates and technical documentation, and coordinating assigned projects, liaising with stakeholders, consultants and contractors to achieve project outcomes.
This is a hands-on position where your technical skills will directly contribute to the development of roads, drainage, and civil infrastructure that supports our vibrant community.
What you’ll be doing:
- Creating and delivering detailed designs and cost estimates for civil infrastructure projects.
- Using Microstation, 12D and other CAD software to complete accurate drawings.
- Undertaking traffic investigations and develop practical solutions.
- Liaising with internal teams, contractors, and consultants to ensure projects run smoothly.
- Providing expert advice on standards, specifications, and policies.
- Conducting site inspections and resolving design-related issues.
What you’ll bring to the role: 
- Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or experience in civil design.
- Strong CAD skills (Microstation and 12D preferred).
- Knowledge of estimating, budgeting, and project administration.
- Excellent communication skills and ability to work collaboratively.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and continuous improvement.
Pre-employment Requirements:
- Current C class driver’s licence
- National Police Clearance not more than six months old
- White Card
- Proof of right to work in Australia

Enquiries: Todd Della Bosca: Senior Technical Officer - Design on (08) 9781 1729 or Human Resources on (08) 9781 1727.
Closing date: Applications are invited until 4.30pm on Monday 26 October 2026. Screening of applications may take place throughout the advertising period.

Immediate Start: Civil Site Engineer – Road Infrastructure
ENGCO Projects is seeking a motivated and experienced Civil Site Engineer to join our growing team on a road infrastructure project in North Melbourne.
ENGCO Projects delivers high-quality engineering, project delivery, safety and commercial services, supporting major civil contractors across Victoria. We provide experienced engineering personnel and integrated project solutions to support the successful delivery of complex civil infrastructure projects.
We are currently seeking a Civil Site Engineer with 2–5 years of site-based experience to support the delivery of road construction and associated civil infrastructure works in North Melbourne.
Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate and supervise day-to-day site engineering activities associated with road construction and civil infrastructure works.
- Oversee construction activities including earthworks, pavement construction, road formation, drainage, underground utilities, service relocations, kerb and channel, footpaths and associated infrastructure.
- Coordinate subcontractors, suppliers and site crews to ensure works are delivered in accordance with project specifications, drawings and construction programs.
- Assist with the coordination, installation and management of underground services and utilities, including service proving, protection, relocations and integration with road construction activities.
- Interpret construction drawings, review design documentation and resolve technical issues in collaboration with project management and design teams.
- Prepare and maintain site documentation, including Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), quality records, daily diaries, permits and progress reports.
- Monitor construction progress, identify potential delays and assist with implementing solutions to maintain project schedules.
- Ensure compliance with project safety, environmental and quality requirements.
- Work closely with project managers, supervisors, surveyors, quality personnel and commercial teams to support efficient project delivery.
Essential Experience & Skills
- Degree-qualified in Civil Engineering or equivalent.
- 2–5 years of site-based experience in civil construction, preferably within road construction or infrastructure projects.
- Current White Card required.
- Demonstrated understanding of road construction methodologies, including earthworks, pavement layers, drainage and underground services.
- Previous utilities experience is highly desirable, particularly exposure to underground service installation, service relocations, service proving and coordination with utility authorities.
- Experience interpreting construction drawings, specifications and project documentation.
- Competent in site engineering, subcontractor coordination, quality assurance and construction reporting.
- Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
- A proactive approach to safety, quality and collaborative project delivery.
Why Join ENGCO Projects?
- Above-industry remuneration packages for the right candidate.
- Opportunity to contribute to the delivery of a road infrastructure project in North Melbourne.
- Work alongside experienced construction and engineering professionals.
- Gain hands-on experience across road construction, earthworks, pavements, drainage and underground utilities.
- Be part of a growing team delivering projects in collaboration with leading civil contractors.
- Develop your technical and project delivery capabilities through practical, site-based experience.
- Potential for permanent employment: High-performing individuals will have the opportunity to be offered full-time positions with ENGCO Projects, subject to performance, project requirements and business needs.
How to Apply
If you are a driven Civil Site Engineer looking to develop your career in road infrastructure delivery, we encourage you to apply. Candidates with previous underground utilities experience are particularly encouraged to express their interest.
This opportunity offers the potential for high-performing candidates to transition into a full-time position with ENGCO Projects, providing an opportunity for long-term career development within our growing team.

candidates.content_text:
Location: Rockhampton
Remuneration/Benefit: Competitive remuneration including overtime. Relocation packages available.
About the role:
Aurizon Network Asset Management is looking for a motivated Civil / Structural Engineer to join our Civil and Structures Assets team and help shape the future of one of Australia’s most important rail networks.
You will contribute to the asset management strategy that connects inland producers with ports along the Queensland coast, from Bowen through Sarina to Gladstone. This is a broad, hands-on role offering exposure to the full asset lifecycle—from understanding asset condition and risk through to shaping renewal scopes, budgets, designs and delivery priorities.
You will help develop capital renewal and maintenance programs across a diverse civil and structures portfolio, including:
- Structures — more than 4,000 culverts, 300 bridges, retaining walls and other structural assets
- Level crossings — more than 700 crossings with a mix of active and passive controls
- Geotechnical and earthworks — steep slopes through several mountain ranges and the formation supporting the track asset
- Access points and access roads — connecting our teams safely and efficiently with railway infrastructure
- Corridor security and fencing — supporting a rail network across an area larger than Tasmania
Working closely with Design Management, Program Management, operations and maintenance teams, you will influence practical, whole-of-business outcomes from concept and design through to delivery of renewal works—balancing safety, risk, track access, cost and scope.
- Influence stakeholders across the business to achieve better outcomes for civil and structures assets
- Assess asset condition, defects and failure modes, applying risk-based engineering judgement to support investment decisions
- Develop renewal and maintenance scopes, budgets and forward programs, and manage changes through planning and delivery
- Improve the processes, tools and data used to make asset management decisions
- Develop and refine strategies, standards, policies and practical engineering guidelines
- Analyse asset information and translate it into clear priorities and recommendations
Around 20% of your time will be spent in the field travelling across the network, giving you direct exposure to the assets you manage and the people who operate and maintain them. The balance offers flexible working across the office and home.
About you:
You are an early-to-mid career Civil or Structural Engineer who is ready to broaden your experience beyond a single project or discipline. You bring experience in design, construction and/or asset management, and you are keen to apply your technical knowledge in a practical operational environment. You enjoy solving complex problems, learning from experienced professionals and working with a wide range of stakeholders to turn sound engineering into real-world outcomes.
Qualifications and experience:
- Bachelor of Civil Engineering or equivalent (mandatory)
- Approximately 2–8 years’ experience in a civil or structural engineering role (mandatory)
- The ability to obtain registration a Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ) in the next 2 years (preferred)
- Experience with rail track infrastructure (desirable, but not essential)
What you will bring:
- A practical understanding of infrastructure operations, design, construction, maintenance and safety requirements
- Clear communication skills and the confidence to consult, negotiate and influence at different levels of the business
- The ability to apply legislation, regulation, standards and engineering requirements in a practical and proportionate way
- Strong written communication skills, with an interest in developing standards, specifications, policies, guidelines and processes
- Commercial awareness and the ability to balance risk, performance, cost and deliverability
If you are ready to accelerate your development, take ownership of a diverse infrastructure portfolio and see the impact of your decisions in the field, we would like to hear from you.
What we offer you:             
At Aurizon, we support the development and growth of our employees. With a national portfolio of operations, we offer long-term and exciting career opportunities. 
Some of our benefits include:
- Development and growth opportunities.
- Access to mentoring and development programs.
- Discounts on selected health insurance funds, personal travel, gyms, vehicles and retail brands.
- Parental leave program and super booster.
About Aurizon.
Aurizon is Australia’s largest rail freight operator and a top 100 ASX company. Each year, we deliver more than 250 million tonnes of Australian commodities right across the country. Aurizon is crucial to the Australian economy, connecting miners, primary producers and industry with international and domestic markets. 
Look to Aurizon for a diverse and collaborative culture.
At Aurizon, we are proud of our diverse, collaborative, creative and high-performance culture. We celebrate the contribution of every employee and provide opportunities for career development in a dynamic, caring, and inclusive work environment.
To learn about us and our company values, please visit www.aurizon.com.au/careers

With award-winning capabilities in dredging, civil contracting, and marine engineering, they pride themselves on their expertise in project management and their strong commitment to clients, employees, and the wider community.

 - Complete conceptual designs of marine structures.

 - Generate and adjust delivery programs (MS Project).

 - Motivated to learn new things and strive for excellence in everything you do.

 - Possess a high level of integrity, honesty and accountability and treat everyone you encounter with utmost respect. 
 - Outstanding communication skills and ability to form strong relationships with people.
 - Available to work full-time during holiday periods.

Benefits

 - You may have the opportunity to work at Hall Contracting as a Graduate Engineer on the completion of your engineering degree.

 - You will work for a company who creates sustainable infrastructure solutions that will be enjoyed for many generations. 
 All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

About Spiire
At Spiire, our purpose is to better our communities, create opportunities for our people and clients, and deliver value to our stakeholders.
We bring together civil and water engineers, landscape architects, construction consultants, surveyors, town planners and urban designers to support the property and infrastructure sectors.
With over 430 employees, we’re one of Australia’s largest employee-owned property and infrastructure consultancies, bringing over 40 years of experience and local expertise to projects across Melbourne, Bendigo, Brisbane, Adelaide, Canberra, Geelong, Ballarat, Shepparton, Gippsland, Albury and Wodonga, and Townsville.
Hello – Kia Ora – 你好 – Wominjeka – Yaama.
No matter how you say it, we’re glad you’re here!
Your engineering career starts here
Planning to study civil engineering in 2027, or already in your first or second year? Join Spiire’s Canberra team and start putting your learning into practice.
We’re looking for an enthusiastic student who’s curious about how communities are designed and built. You don’t need previous industry experience—just a willingness to learn, ask questions and get involved.
With paid employment, financial study support and guidance from experienced colleagues, this is an opportunity to build your confidence and explore a future in civil engineering.
About Spiire
We’re an integrated team of engineers, surveyors, planners, landscape architects and other property and infrastructure specialists. We bring different disciplines together to help shape communities.
In Canberra, you’ll join a supportive team and gain an introduction to civil engineering within a multidisciplinary consultancy.
What you’ll be doing
Working alongside our engineers, you’ll build your understanding of how civil projects move from design through to delivery. As your skills develop, you’ll have opportunities to:
 - 
 Assist with engineering tasks, project documentation and technical information.
 - 
 Learn about civil design and the infrastructure that supports land development.
 - 
 Gain exposure to project coordination and how we work with clients and other disciplines.
 - 
 Participate in site visits where project requirements allow.
 - 
 Apply what you’re learning at university to practical engineering work.
About you
We’d love to hear from you if you’re:
 - 
 A school leaver planning to commence engineering studies in 2027, with an interest in civil engineering; or
 - 
 A current first-year engineering student intending to pursue civil engineering, or a second-year civil engineering student.
You’ll bring a positive attitude, clear communication and an interest in working with others. You’ll also be comfortable asking questions and taking on new challenges.
We’re particularly keen to connect with students from Canberra and the surrounding region, including those studying elsewhere who return home during university breaks and are interested in building their career locally.
Work that supports your studies
The opportunity includes paid work in our Canberra office, with an anticipated summer commitment of two to three days per week during December and January. We’ll discuss your availability and study commitments with you.
You’ll also receive $5,000 gross annual study support, subject to the terms of your study support agreement.
Ready to get started?
Apply with your CV and a short cover letter telling us:
 - 
 What you’re studying, or planning to study in 2027.
 - 
 Why you’re interested in civil engineering.
 - 
 Your connection to Canberra and availability over summer.
Your CV can include school projects, part-time work, volunteering or extracurricular activities—we’re interested in your potential and enthusiasm to learn.
Our Culture, Our Difference
At Spiire, we believe our culture is our difference. As a successful and growing employee-owned business, we recognise and reward the contributions of our people and provide real opportunities and pathways for career progression.
Here’s a snapshot of what’s on offer:
 - Structured training, knowledge-sharing forums and mentoring opportunities.
 - Supportive leaders and clear pathways for career development.
 - Collaboration with technical specialists across disciplines and offices.
 - Health and wellbeing initiatives supporting physical, emotional, social and financial wellbeing.
 - Extended leave benefits, including study leave and volunteer days.
 - An inclusive, connected team culture with regular social and office events.
InSpiire to build something great
If this sounds like your next move, we’d love to hear from you.
For questions about the role or recruitment process, please contact Spiire.Careers@spiire.com.au.
Apply now or discover more about us at www.spiire.com.au.

Civil Engineering Graduate - 2027 Graduate Program
Go places with Fulton Hogan
You've probably seen our work on roads, bridges, airports, water projects, telecommunications networks and community infrastructure right across Australia. We build and maintain the infrastructure that keeps people moving and communities connected.
We're looking for Civil Engineering Graduates to join our 2027 Graduate Program in Launceston This is a role for someone who wants to be out where the work happens, learning from experienced people and delivering projects that leave a lasting impact.
From day one, you'll be out on infrastructure projects, working alongside site teams to help plan, coordinate and deliver construction work. Safety, quality, environment, cost, programme and community outcomes are all part of the picture, and you'll learn how they fit together in practice.
What our Graduate Program offers
Our Graduate Program gives you structure, support and plenty of opportunity to learn. You'll be part of a 12-month program with exposure to fast-paced environments where no two days are quite the same.
You can expect:
- A Career Development Framework to help guide your growth
- A buddy to help with day-to-day questions
- Graduate networking and development sessions
- A regional welcome and annual Grad induction
About you
You'll bring:
- A relevant Civil Engineering qualification
- Practical decision-making skills
- A hands-on approach and commitment to working safely
- Strong communication and teamwork
- Curiosity, resilience and drive
- Flexibility to travel, work occasional weekends or night shift, and relocate for career opportunities where required
- Alignment with our values: Respect, Energy & Effort, Attitude and Leadership.
Eligibility
To be eligible, you must:
- Be currently residing in Launceston or the surrounding areas
- Be an Australian Permanent Resident or Citizen
- Have completed a relevant undergraduate degree in the last two years, or be due to complete your studies before February 2027
- Have achieved a minimum overall weighted average mark (WAM) of 65 out of 100
Next steps
Apply online with your CV and cover letter. Successful candidates will also need to complete pre-employment checks before receiving a formal offer to join our 2027 Graduate Program.
Start your career journey with Fulton Hogan.

ACCIONA is a global company, leading in the development of regenerative infrastructure that creates a positive impact on society. Our workforce consists of more than 65,000 professionals, present in more than 40 countries across the five continents, all contributing to our mission to design a better planet. Are you a passionate individual who wants to make a difference, promote sustainable development, and find solutions to the biggest global challenges, including climate change, overpopulation, and water scarcity? Come and join us in building the infrastructure our planet needs to achieve a sustainable future.
Geotech, one of Acciona' s specialist businesses with over fifty years of experience at the frontlines of design and delivery. The range of expertise includes foundation piling, basement construction, ground improvement, ground anchors, water infrastructure construction and more.
As one of Australia's largest and most diversely skilled engineering and construction contracting business, Geotech has the capabilities to be a single contractor to a broad spectrum of clients, delivering the full scope of works.
About Opportunity
We are looking for a Graduate Engineer to join our Geotech business, this role requires you to have total flexibility and able to support projects across Australia in regional locations.
When on site you will receive Living Away From Home allowances and project allowances. 
You will deliver the full range of a ground and foundation engineer's responsibilities across piling, ground anchoring and ground improvement works, from safety and construction documentation through to procurement, budget tracking, services and utilities investigation, and specialist testing.
Key accountabilities
- Identify the whole-of-life aspects of infrastructure being delivered
- Identify project specifications and draft inspection and test plans (ITPs) to ensure verification of compliance with the contract
- Administer bored pile, CFA, driven, sheet piling and ground improvement works to safety, environmental and quality requirements
- Administer ground anchoring, soil nails, slope stabilisation and grout curtain works to safety, environmental and quality requirements
- Develop and implement construction procedures for piling, ground anchors, soil nailing and ground improvement
- Investigate services and utilities and issue internal permits to work
- Prepare Work Procedures, ITPs, SWMS and Site Access Plans for specialist ground works
- Coordinate pile integrity testing, static and dynamic load testing, and anchor proof and lock off testing
- Prepare, track and forecast construction budgets, and manage daily cost control
- Record daily progress, deliveries, resourcing, delays, variations and day works accurately
Qualification and Competencies 
- Civil Engineering degree or similar, with a geotechnical focus (Must have graduate by January 2027)
- Ideally exposure in foundation construction activities for transmission line and major infrastructure projects, including piling, stub setting, excavation, reinforcement installation, concreting, and associated ground engineering works highly desirable
- Current driver licence and access to a reliable vehicle
- Ability to achieve a successful Pre-Employment Medical and National Crime Check is required.

candidates.content_text:
JMT Civil are seeking an experienced Civil Estimator to join our growing civil construction team. This role plays a critical part in securing work across a diverse pipeline of civil projects and working closely with leadership to price work that is both competitive and commercially sound.
You’ll be responsible for the end-to-end tender process, from initial review and pricing through to handover to delivery teams once a project is awarded.
About the role
As a Civil Estimator, you will:
- Review and interpret tender documents, drawings, and specifications
- Complete detailed quantity take-offs across:
- Earthworks
- Drainage & utilities
- Roadworks
- Civil structures
- Prepare accurate, first-principles cost estimates for labour, plant, materials, and subcontractors
- Source, analyse, and negotiate subcontractor and supplier pricing
- Identify risks, constraints, assumptions, and contingencies within tenders
- Assist with tender submissions, including pricing schedules and methodology input
- Provide value-engineering options to optimise cost and constructability
- Attend site inspections where required to assess conditions impacting pricing
- Maintain estimating rates, cost databases, and historical pricing records
- Conduct detailed handovers of successful tenders to project delivery teams
About you
You’ll bring strong civil construction knowledge and commercial awareness, along with:
- 5+ years’ experience in Civil Estimating
- A degree in Civil Engineering or relevant tertiary qualification
- Experience across subdivisions, earthworks, roadworks, utilities, and civil infrastructure
- Exposure to TfNSW projects highly regarded
- Strong understanding of first-principles estimating
- Excellent attention to detail with strong negotiation and communication skills
- Ability to manage multiple tenders and deadlines simultaneously
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel essential); AutoCAD experience advantageous
- Current Australian driver’s licence
What we offer
- Competitive salary package with performance incentives
- Stable pipeline of civil works with long-term career opportunities
- Supportive, team-focused culture with experienced professionals
- Ongoing training and professional development
- Regular team events
About us
We are a well-established civil contractor delivering quality projects with a strong focus on people, safety, and long-term relationships. Our culture is practical, professional, and built on trust — we value people who take ownership and want to grow with the business.
If you’re a Civil Estimator looking for your next step in a supportive and forward-moving team, we’d love to hear from you.
Apply now with your resume outlining your estimating experience and project background.

The proposed project consists of a program of works across three Department of Defence establishments including:
- Albury Wodonga Military Area (including North, South & East Bandiana, Latchford Barracks, Wirlinga)
- Blamey Barracks (Kapooka)
- RAAF Base Wagga
The proposed capital investment of $2 billion will incorporate a variety of elements including:
- Construction of new messing and living in accommodation
- Construction of new training facilities
- Refurbishment and upgrading of existing buildings
- Remedial works and upgrades to infrastructure services
To review all Downer opportunities on the Riverina Deployment Joint Venture (RRJV) please visit the website: Downer in the NSW Riverina - Downer Group Australia
The opportunity
We are seeking a Site Engineer - Services Infrastructure to support the delivery of critical Defence services works at Blamey Barracks Kapooka. Working closely with the Project Engineer, this role will assist in managing the installation of key services infrastructure packages, ensuring works are delivered safely, to quality standards and in line with RRJV systems. This is an excellent opportunity for a developing engineer to gain experience on a tier 1 Defence infrastructure program.
What you'll do
- Support the Project Engineer with the delivery of services infrastructure works including HV electrical, potable water, fire water and sewer mains
- Coordinate subcontractors to ensure works are delivered safely on program and to specification
- Assist with resolving design and constructability issues on site
- Support quality control activities, inspections and documentation
- Assist with commissioning and handover activities for completed services packages
What you'll bring
- Degree qualification in Services Engineering (Electrical, Mechanical, Hydraulic or Building Services) or Civil Engineering
- Exposure to services infrastructure installations in a site or graduate engineering role
- Understanding of subcontractor coordination and site-quality processes
- Strong communication skills and the ability to work within a multidisciplinary project team
- Experience on construction or infrastructure projects (Defence experience advantageous but not essential)
This role is based at Wagga Wagga. Relocation assistance is available for the successful candidate if required. This is not a DIDO or FIFO role, applicants must be willing to relocate, be an Australian citizen and willing to obtain a security clearance.
Spotless Management Services Pty Ltd (a Downer Company) is delivering the works as part of a joint venture with CPB Contractors Pty Ltd. Accordingly we will share your Personal Information, to the extent necessary, for the purpose of recruitment for the joint venture with CPB Contractors Pty Ltd who are required to handle that information in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

At Downer, we plan, create, and sustain essential public services across Australia and New Zealand. From hospitals to data centres and defence partnerships, we manage critical infrastructure that keeps communities thriving.

- With 30% of vacancies filled internally you'll find real opportunities to advance your career.
- Perks@Downer: healthcare discounts, great savings on retail purchases, car purchases and much more.

We believe our people are our greatest asset, which is why we invest in their wellbeing, development, and success.
Our employees enjoy competitive remuneration, professional development opportunities, career progression pathways, flexible work arrangements where appropriate, health and wellbeing initiatives, employee recognition programs, social and team events, and opportunities to contribute to meaningful community and sustainability initiatives.
At Guidera O’Connor, you’ll be supported to build a rewarding career while maintaining a healthy balance between work and life.

- Assist in providing technical input on design, construction methods, program modifications, and structural repairs to support project delivery.
- Support procurement activities and contribute to the coordination and management of suppliers and subcontractors.
- Identify project issues, investigate root causes, and contribute to practical solutions while understanding how project components influence overall outcomes.
- Work collaboratively within the team to maintain a safe, inclusive, and compliant work environment, supporting HSEQ standards, team learning, and continuous personal development.
To be successful, you will have experience and demonstrate capability in the following:
- Tertiary qualifications in Bachelor of Civil Engineering or similar
- 2-5 years of relevant experience in a construction industry
- TfNSW roads experience
- Ability to obtain a National Police Clearence
- White Card - CPCWHS1001 Prepare to Work Safely in the Construction Industry
- Valid Driver’s License
WHY JOIN ERTECH?
At Ertech, we’re committed to investing in our people and creating a workplace where you can thrive. Here’s what you can look forward to: 
- Competitive remuneration
- An opportunity to join a growing business in NSW and have a real impact on its success.
- Full-time position offering stability and annual leave entitlements
- Supportive, team-oriented culture where collaboration and respect are valued 
- Career development and progression opportunities, annual performance development plans.
- Access to great benefits, including: 
- Discounted Private Health Insurance (HBF & Medibank)
- Annual flu vaccinations 
- Novated leasing options through Paywise
- Service recognition and milestone rewards 
- Employee Referral Program incentives 
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family.
OUR CULTURE
At Ertech, our people are fundamental to our success. We're focused on creating an inclusive workplace, with the right people in the right roles, who are engaged, empowered, and appropriately rewarded. Ertech will provide you with the chance to be a part of great team, meet new people and gain experience with an industry leader who puts safety first. 
DIVERSITY & INCLUSION
We value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives of all people and actively encourage applications from First Nations peoples, all genders, culturally and linguistically diverse individuals, people with disability, LGBTQIA+ community members, and veterans of the Australian Defence Force.
Ertech is a proud Veteran Employment supporter. We recognise the valuable skills and leadership that veterans bring to our industry and welcome their applications at all levels of the business. Even if you don’t meet every requirement listed, we encourage you to apply and bring your strengths to our team.
HOW TO APPLY
Click "Apply" on this job advertisement, which will direct you to Ertech's application portal. Simply follow the steps outlined on the portal to complete your application.
This is an incredible opportunity! If you are looking for a position in an environment in which you can flourish whilst building your career, there is no better time to join the Ertech Team than now!
